solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Somewhere to discuss university cutting class? (5)

indicatorNotes.cutting: the U cuts into FORM, splitting it open

blocks.note: a school class is a form
U is the standard abbreviation for university

annotation.surface: A student skips a lesson to go and argue somewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutting class' reads as skipping school; here class is FORM (a British school year group) and the university letter cuts through it.
annotation.definitionFit: A forum is a place or meeting set up for discussion.

entries.clue: Pastry enthusiast welcoming learner (4)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: FAN takes the L in, as a host welcomes a guest

blocks.note: L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

annotation.surface: A pastry lover takes a beginner under their wing.
annotation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates new drivers display in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a filling.

entries.clue: Bar means of transport (4)

blocks.note: a bar as on a fence or a towel holder
the railway as a way of travelling

annotation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a pub, but it is the metal or wooden rod.
annotation.definitionFit: A rail is both a horizontal bar and, by extension, the railway network you travel on.

entries.clue: Object from space encountered below at intervals? Correct, we hear (9)

indicatorNotes.at intervals: take letters at regular gaps: the 2nd and 4th of BELOW
indicatorNotes.we hear: what we hear is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: right = correct, which sounds like RITE

annotation.surface: Someone spots a thing from space overhead and asks for confirmation.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose picture; the pieces ignore the surface entirely.
annotation.definitionFit: A meteorite is a rock from space that has reached the ground.

entries.clue: Conservative girl in charge in Derby? (7)

annotation.surface: A Tory woman takes charge of affairs in the city of Derby.
annotation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the English town, but it is the horse race: the Derby is one of Britain's five Classics, flat races for three-year-olds. The question mark marks it as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: The Derby is one of the English Classic horse races, so it is a classic.

entries.clue: Italian city supporting Church element that shines (6)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down answer ROME sits beneath CH, holding it up

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

annotation.surface: An Italian city backs the Church, a shining light.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supporting' only works in a down clue: the supporter goes underneath.
annotation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium, a metallic element prized for its bright shine.

entries.clue: Purpose of action is missed first of all (3)

indicatorNotes.first of all: take the first letter of all the words before it

annotation.surface: A plan is lost because nobody acted first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Missed' reads as a failure; it only supplies its M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what you aim at is the purpose behind what you do.

entries.clue: Cloth worker becoming police officer (8)

blocks.note: the worker ant: a crossword staple

annotation.surface: A textile worker changes career and joins the police.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cloth worker' reads as one person; split it into the fabric and the insect.
annotation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a police officer ranking above a constable.

entries.clue: Note new picture is less expensive (3-5)

indicatorNotes.new: the letters of PICTURE are made into something new

annotation.surface: A memo says a new painting is going cheap.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram covers PICTURE only; the note C goes in front.
annotation.definitionFit: Cut-price goods are sold at reduced prices, so less expensive.

entries.clue: Pilot beginning to advance by way of hill (7)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the first letter of ADVANCE

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

annotation.surface: A pilot starts moving forward over a hill.
annotation.walkthrough: TOR is a craggy hill in the southwest of England, common in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly old-fashioned: aviator is the formal word for someone who flies aircraft.

entries.clue: Excellence of French waters, exactly what’s needed (5)

blocks.note: la mer is French for the sea

annotation.surface: The fine quality of French seas is just what someone wants.
annotation.walkthrough: IT as 'exactly what's needed' is the sense in 'this is it!'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: merit is the quality of deserving praise, which is excellence.

entries.clue: Unusual demo car men seize (10)

indicatorNotes.Unusual: the letters are put in an unusual order

annotation.surface: Some men take over an odd demonstration vehicle.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a commandeering: men grabbing a car.
annotation.definitionFit: To commandeer is to seize, especially for official use.

entries.clue: Plant US drugs policeman is at the outset setting up secretly (9)

indicatorNotes.at the outset: take the start of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: narc is American slang for a narcotics agent

annotation.surface: An American narcotics officer covertly plants evidence at the start of an operation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' sits at the front like the verb for framing someone, which suits a drugs cop; it is the flower.
annotation.definitionFit: Narcissus is the plant genus that includes daffodils.

entries.clue: Aesthetically pleasing section of chart is ticked (8)

indicatorNotes.section of: the answer is a stretch cut from the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of chart, all of is and the start of ticked

annotation.surface: Part of a chart has been checked off and looks nice.
annotation.definitionFit: Artistic can mean attractive in a tasteful, aesthetic way.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three words, starting after the CH of chart and ending before the KED of ticked.

entries.clue: Power or composure this sea creature has (8)

annotation.surface: A sea animal is credited with strength and calm.
annotation.walkthrough: Read it backwards: this sea creature has P, OR and POISE in it.
annotation.definitionFit: The porpoise is a small toothed whale.

entries.clue: Bookmaker getting new starter, this inexperienced person? (6)

indicatorNotes.getting new starter: the first letter of BOOKIE is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: the new first letter replaces the B; the clue leaves it to the crossings

annotation.surface: A betting shop takes on a beginner.
annotation.walkthrough: Nothing names the new letter: once you see BOOKIE, the only word meaning a novice with a fresh first letter is ROOKIE.
annotation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer with little experience.

entries.clue: Like some humour found in Cairo, nice (6)

indicatorNotes.found in: the answer is found in the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of Cairo and the start of nice; ignore the comma

annotation.surface: Someone finds jokes in Cairo and the French city of Nice.
annotation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the Riviera city or the adjective; it just lends its first three letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Ironic humour says the opposite of what it means.

entries.clue: Holidaymaker’s escapade entertaining Mike (6)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: CAPER holds M inside, as a host entertains a guest

blocks.note: a caper is a lively escapade
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A holidaymaker's jaunt amuses someone called Mike.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is', joining definition to wordplay, not a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A camper is someone holidaying in a tent or camper van.

entries.clue: Organising opera, sir? I’m someone who maybe can help? (10)

indicatorNotes.Organising: the letters are organised into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone offers to help a gentleman put on an opera.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is vague on its own; the surface supplies the rest, since organising opera is exactly an impresario's job.
annotation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and finances operas and concerts, so could help with one.

entries.clue: Time everyone finds hard to believe (4)

annotation.surface: Eventually everyone finds something incredible.
annotation.walkthrough: TALL means hard to believe as in a tall story or tall tale.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: tall means exaggerated or implausible only in phrases like a tall story or tall tale.

entries.clue: Gamble full of Northern flair (4)

indicatorNotes.full of: something full of a thing has it inside, so BET holds the N within it

annotation.surface: A wager shows real northern style.
annotation.walkthrough: BENT here is a natural aptitude, as in 'an artistic bent'.
annotation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural talent or flair for something.

entries.clue: One stealing article I put inside, fearful initially (5)

indicatorNotes.put inside: the I is put inside the article, placed within THE between its H and E
indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of FEARFUL

annotation.surface: A nervous burglar sneaks an item back indoors.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: 'one stealing' describes the person rather than naming them, which is what a thief is.
annotation.walkthrough: The article is THE, the definite article; 'put inside' applies to I, which goes into it before the F is added.

entries.clue: In good health, suitable (3)

blocks.note: healthy and in good condition, as after exercise
appropriate or right for a purpose

annotation.definitionFit: The word covers both healthy physical condition and being right for a purpose.
annotation.walkthrough: Two plain meanings side by side with a comma between; no wordplay beyond that.

entries.clue: Get through exam period — a journey (7)

blocks.note: to pass an exam is to get through it
an age is a period of time

annotation.surface: A student sees passing exams as one long trek.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash makes the wordplay look like a heading; the definition is 'a journey', as in a sea passage.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the travel sense: a passage is a voyage, as in booking a passage to America.

entries.clue: After review rector accommodating a person who’s inventive (7)

indicatorNotes.After review: RECTOR is reworked into a new order
indicatorNotes.accommodating: the rearranged letters take the A in

annotation.surface: Following an inspection, a clergyman puts up an ingenious lodger.
annotation.walkthrough: A rector is a parish priest; the church setting hints at the Creator, but here it just means an inventive person.
annotation.definitionFit: A creator is someone who invents or makes things.

entries.clue: Leave resort in Croatia (5)

blocks.note: slang for to go away, depart
a coastal city and holiday destination in Croatia

annotation.walkthrough: Split is a port and holiday city on Croatia's Adriatic coast.
annotation.definitionFit: Split means to leave in slang, and is a Croatian resort.
